top_papers.abstract: PlayTrain is an efficient reinforcement learning framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate adaptable JavaScript games from simple prompts. Its core method involves using LLMs for game creation and a pipeline to integrate these games into a standard RL environment. This framework's contribution lies in significantly reducing the manual effort required to create and adapt game environments for RL training, enabling high-throughput agent learning on novel or modified games.
top_papers.figure_caption: A: The concept of PlayTrain: Through LLM-generated JS code, PlayTrain can transform games such as “DownWell” and “VVVVVV” into an RL environment and train agents in minutes. B: The generation pipeline. From a short specification of a video game, an LLM generates a single self-contained JavaScript file against a fixed RL-environment prompt-file, creating an environment that is both immediately playable and ready for baseline RL agent training without any additional code.

top_papers.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the emergent collective behavior of AI agents that spontaneously used a public wiki for cooperation. The core method involves analyzing the agents' edit history to understand their decision-making process. The key contribution is the discovery that agents primarily copy existing content, with their choices heavily influenced by what they observe on the current page and recent edits, explaining their coordinated actions without explicit instruction.

top_papers.title: Global Divergence, Local Convergence: Representation Geometry in SSMs and Transformers
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the geometric differences in internal representations between State-Space Models (SSMs) and Transformers. It reveals that SSMs distribute information evenly across dimensions, while Transformers concentrate it along a dominant direction, a trend amplified by attention layers. This geometric divergence impacts representational capacity and compressibility, with SSMs showing surprising advantages despite their different structure.
top_papers.figure_caption: PCA of representations from Pythia and Mamba over a subset of the LAMA TREx dataset. Mamba’s representations are more spread out across the space.

top_papers.title: Active Adaptation, Not Static Defense: Temporal Dynamics of Preventative Steering in Adversarial Fine-Tuning
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the temporal dynamics of Preventative Steering, a defense against adversarial fine-tuning in LLMs. It reveals that the defense relies on an **active adaptation process** during training, rather than a static injection of corrective signals. The core contribution is demonstrating that the protection fades if the learned weight offsets are simply preserved or reinjected, highlighting the importance of ongoing adaptation and leading to the proposal of a new defense strategy, Progressive Intensity Scheduling.
top_papers.figure_caption: Mechanistic dynamics of gradient drift and the Progressive Intensity Scheduling (PIS) defense. Phase I (Left): In the backward pass, the injected + v m +v_{m} induces adversarial tension, which the optimizer absorbs via structural − v m -v_{m} shifts (Mechanism A). This adaptation is structurally asymmetric: the output projection ( W o W_{o} ) shifts unrestrictedly, while the down projection ( W down W_{\( \mathrm{down} \)} ) is constrained by SiLU activation sparsity. These strictly process-dependent static offsets provide no standalone defense (Mechanism B). Phase II (Right): Over optimization steps, the adversarial gradient ( ∇ L adv \( \nabla \) L_{\( \mathrm{adv} \)} ) drifts from its initial v m v_{m} -alignment via optimizer adaptation (Mechanism C), dismantling the gradient-absorbing equilibrium. To counteract this decay, PIS temporally scales injection strength ( \( \alpha \) ) to restore compensatory pressure against malicious fine-tuning.

top_papers.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Sample-Adaptive Strategy Routing for Vision Token Pruning in MLLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the inefficiency of processing numerous visual tokens in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by proposing VIP-Router. Instead of a single fixed pruning strategy, VIP-Router adaptively selects the best pruning method for each input based on its visual and textual features. This sample-adaptive approach improves efficiency by avoiding suboptimal pruning and retaining full token processing when beneficial.
top_papers.figure_caption: (a) The accuracy-best strategy varies across the full VTC-Bench Group A and reduction ratios, with no strategy winning more than half of the 40 benchmark-ratio settings. (b) At each reduction ratio, the stacked bars split Group A samples into those answered correctly by Best Fixed, those missed by Best Fixed but answered correctly by another strategy, and those missed by all strategies. Purple dots report the fraction of samples solvable by at least one strategy that are wrong with Best Fixed, which exceeds one-third at every ratio. (c) In this example, Qwen2-VL yields contrasting predictions across different pruning strategies, illustrating their inherent complementarity.

top_papers.title: Beyond Surface Imitation: Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment in Multimodal In-Context Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel multimodal in-context learning (ICL) framework that moves beyond superficial imitation. It introduces contrastive demonstration modeling, where demonstrations explicitly highlight the difference between suboptimal and optimal responses along with the reasoning path for refinement. This approach aims to align MLLMs with the correct reasoning process, improving performance on complex multimodal tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. From surface level imitation to reasoning path alignment. Standard multimodal ICL mainly aligns the final output and may imitate surface patterns from visually similar demonstrations. In contrast, COMIL uses contrastive demonstrations to make explicit which visual evidence is relevant and how the current response should be revised, thereby guiding the MLLM toward the desired reasoning path. Comparison between standard multimodal ICL and COMIL, illustrating how contrastive demonstrations and refinement guidance move the model from surface imitation toward evidence-grounded reasoning path alignment.

top_papers.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether foundation models can effectively moderate online content by comparing instruction-driven and example-driven policy operationalization. Using the new ModerationBench benchmark, they demonstrate that foundation models significantly outperform existing systems, achieving comparable effectiveness with both guidance approaches. This suggests foundation models hold promise for more consistent and accurate content moderation.

top_papers.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: ConvMem addresses LLM limitations with long contexts by reformulating reasoning as a hierarchical convolution, treating the LLM as a kernel. This training-free, parallelizable method summarizes text segments in a logarithmic tree structure, significantly reducing latency compared to sequential approaches. Its key contribution is enabling efficient long-context reasoning without costly RL training.
top_papers.figure_caption: Illustration of the hierarchical convolutional mechanism within a single channel. At Layer 0, the semantic kernel 𝒦 \( \mathcal{K} \) scans raw text segments in parallel to generate condensed summaries. Subsequent layers recursively process the concatenated summaries from the previous layer. After L L layers, the global summary is combined with critical raw segments (skip connections) to generate the final answer A A .

top_papers.title: Direct Diversity Optimization for Diverse Successful Trajectories in Preference Post-Training
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of training LLM agents to discover multiple successful strategies from a single decision point. Their proposed method, Direct Diversity Optimization (DDO), combines a novel tree-based collection of diverse trajectories with a reference-relative objective. DDO effectively improves both task success and the coverage of different successful strategies, outperforming existing methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: A motivating online-shopping example: Model A, a standard post-trained model, completes the purchase through a single trajectory, while Model B retains multiple successful trajectories that can be used as fallbacks when conditions change.

top_papers.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes FOM-UL, a layer-selective unlearning method for LLMs. It identifies and updates only the most influential transformer layers for forgetting specific data, minimizing impact on the rest of the model. This targeted approach improves the balance between forgetting unwanted information and maintaining model utility, even after post-training quantization.
top_papers.figure_caption: FOM-UL robust and quantization-resilient forgetting against global and partial unlearning methods.

top_papers.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework for geometric reasoning using a Large Language Model (LLM) by integrating a Geometric Vision Parser and a Symbolic Solver. The parser translates geometric diagrams into symbolic representations, which the solver then uses for logical deduction. This approach achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art multimodal models while offering more interpretable and human-like solutions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Schematic representation of the pipeline.

top_papers.title: RAP: Research Attention Prediction Reveals Target-Conditioned Evidence Acquisition Biases
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Research Attention Prediction (RAP), a novel benchmark for evaluating LLMs as research agents by predicting future paper shares across AI/ML fields. The core contribution is identifying that LLMs struggle to accurately predict research trends, often underperforming a simple moving average baseline, and revealing that their evidence acquisition strategies, particularly how they carry forward past information, are key to this limitation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Compared to literature review, which surveys and summarises existing scientific records in a certain field, Research Attention Prediction (RAP) predicts the distribution of scientific activity in that field in the near future (e.g. six months).

top_papers.title: TRACE: Training Reasoning Agents for Causal Exploration with Synthesized Rewards
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces TRACE, a method for training reasoning agents in complex diagnostic tasks where ground truth is hard to obtain. TRACE synthesizes verifiable rewards by simulating interventions in a controlled environment, allowing agents to learn causal reasoning from noisy, real-world-like data. The core contribution is demonstrating how to engineer objective rewards for diagnostic tasks, overcoming the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning in domains lacking easily verifiable answers.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the TRACE workflow.

top_papers.title: What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RD-Forget, a training-free framework that separates an agent's stored experience from its active memory. It achieves this by maintaining a source archive and a query-conditioned memory view, allowing superseded facts to be retained for historical context while suppressing them for current queries. The core contribution is a novel method for managing long-term memory in language agents, enabling them to recall past information while providing relevant, up-to-date answers.

top_papers.title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel evaluation protocol for time-series foundation models by creating a test set of data published *after* model training. The core contribution is demonstrating that pretrained models still outperform others on this "later" test set, suggesting their familiarity with the training data, not just a new domain, is key to their success. However, intrinsic data properties like seasonal strength don't explain why pretrained models win in some cases but not others.
top_papers.figure_caption: Average rank with Nemenyi intervals, per group. Any model whose interval crosses the dashed line is statistically indistinguishable from the best model in that panel. Exchange rates, on the bottom row, is the panel where every interval overlaps every other and the Friedman test does not reject.

top_papers.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
top_papers.abstract: Maverick enables private and verifiable LLM inference by delegating the computationally intensive matrix-vector multiplication operation. Its core contribution is an information-theoretically sound verification protocol for this delegation, offering transparent preprocessing, efficient verification, and minimal server overhead, thus addressing privacy and correctness concerns without requiring users to run large models locally.

top_papers.title: $Φ$-Bench: Can Large Language Models Engineer the Infrastructure That Powers Them?
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces $Φ$-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to engineer the infrastructure that supports them. Unlike previous benchmarks, $Φ$-Bench covers the entire LLM infrastructure stack with tasks ranging from kernel optimization to system-level improvements, addressing the need for evaluating open-ended, long-horizon engineering capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Performance of frontier models on \( \Phi \) -Bench. Left : Overall scores achieved by different models. Right : Model performance across different infrastructure topics.

top_papers.title: ProbPlug: A Plugin Uncertainty Network for Reliable Confidence in LLM Binary Classification
top_papers.abstract: ProbPlug is a lightweight framework that estimates the confidence of LLM binary classification predictions by analyzing internal token features from a frozen LLM. It uses a self-attention module to aggregate these features, providing reliable confidence estimates without altering the base model. This approach improves classification performance with minimal overhead and generalizes well across different tasks and model types.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivation for the proposed method. (a) Traditional LLM inference relies on next-token probabilities, which are often poorly calibrated and difficult to threshold in high-stakes settings. (b) ProbPlug estimates confidence from multi-layer hidden representations of a frozen LLM, enabling reliable and flexible threshold-based filtering.

top_papers.title: The Answer Path and the Grounding Instruction in LLM Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how to best present knowledge graph triples to Large Language Models for question answering. The core method involves systematically varying four aspects of the prompt: the triples included (specifically, the "answer path"), their syntax, their order, and a grounding instruction. The key contribution is demonstrating that including the answer path is crucial for performance, while the grounding instruction has a significant positive impact, whereas syntax and order have minimal effect.

top_papers.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper surveys inference-efficiency mechanisms for VideoLLMs, which are expensive due to their computational demands. The core contribution is a structured analysis of techniques that reduce parameter count, FLOPs, latency, and memory usage across different stages of the VideoLLM pipeline, from frame sampling to LLM decoding. This work aims to make VideoLLMs more deployable in resource-constrained environments.

top_papers.title: Artificial Id: Drive and Persistent Alignment in Agentic AI
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces an "artificial id" as an internal, adaptive drive for agentic AI systems. This mechanism allows agents to autonomously decide when to continue, stop, or change their behavior, moving beyond externally defined control. The core contribution is demonstrating that such adaptive direction and persistent alignment can emerge organically through differential persistence, even in agents lacking general reasoning capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Functional architecture of the artificial id. Current language models provide the general reasoning associated here with the ego. The experiment isolates a minimal adaptive drive whose behavior is shaped through differential persistence in an environment. In the proposed coupled architecture, the id influences what the system continues to pursue, the ego translates that state into task-specific reasoning and action, and the resulting changes to the system and its environment become new input to the id. The right panel situates this loop within a persistent alignment boundary. Across the proposed architecture, that boundary comprises trusted observations, consequence channels, persistent state, authority, identity, provenance and hard constraints. Variation and differential persistence are the learning mechanism used in the experiment to produce adaptive drive; they are not required components of the proposed deployed id. The integrated architecture is proposed and is not tested here.

top_papers.title: Autonomy, Social Norms, and Alignment: Towards a Developmental Framework for Autonomous Artificial Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a developmental framework for autonomous AI agents, moving beyond static datasets to enable learning through environmental interaction. Its core method involves incorporating intrinsic motivations like curiosity and competence to guide exploration, thereby enhancing autonomy. The key contribution is addressing the complex challenge of aligning these increasingly independent agents with human goals in dynamic, unstructured environments.

top_papers.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in LLM-generated text, combining a fine-tuned classifier, Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty, and temperature scaling. The core contribution is a robust detection method that achieves high accuracy on various tasks and demonstrates genuine reasoning capabilities, not just pattern matching. Additionally, the work shows that a significant portion of performance can be achieved with limited training data and applies DPO to reduce hallucinations in a generator model.

top_papers.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: Ecdysis addresses the inefficiency of training LLM agent runtime harnesses by introducing principled failure diagnosis. Instead of simply iterating on observed failures, Ecdysis distinguishes between model-specific and harness-specific issues. This allows for more targeted and efficient optimization of the harness, leading to improved generalization and reduced training time.

top_papers.title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation
top_papers.abstract: LOCUS is a task-aware, low-rank adaptation method for post-training large language models. It efficiently minimizes generation length by adapting only a small subspace of parameters, thereby reducing serving costs without sacrificing response utility. This approach achieves significant length reductions while updating a minimal fraction of the model's parameters.

top_papers.title: MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution
top_papers.abstract: MAPLE is a system that helps domain experts solve optimization problems using natural language. Its core method combines language understanding, mathematical programming, and evolutionary search to create and adapt optimization models. MAPLE's contribution is enabling rapid, iterative updates to optimization problems by remembering past decisions and search results, making optimization more accessible and adaptable to dynamic real-world scenarios.
top_papers.figure_caption: MAPLE maintains plans through successive requests. The routing example shows problem revision, memory of earlier decisions, and reuse of search results. The tables compare capabilities and performance. An asterisk marks adapted baselines.

top_papers.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MindTopo, a benchmark designed to evaluate foundation models' ability to reason about topological spatial relations, which are invariant under continuous deformation. The benchmark covers five cognitive properties (continuity, separation, order, enclosure, knots) at two levels (reasoning and planning) and contains over 11,000 instances. MindTopo's contribution is to shift the focus of foundation model evaluation from metric properties to the more fundamental topological aspects of spatial understanding.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of MindTopo . Five topological properties ( continuity , separation , order , enclosure , knots ) probed at two cognitive levels: reasoning (visual QA over rendered scenes) and planning (interactive gym).

top_papers.title: RetroThinker: Enabling Retrospective Thinking in Speech LLMs
top_papers.abstract: RetroThinker enables streaming SpeechLLMs to improve their reasoning by dynamically revising their thought processes during inference. It achieves this through a post-training framework that combines supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization, allowing the model to self-verify and correct its reasoning steps on the fly. This approach aims to overcome the accuracy-latency trade-off in SpeechLLMs for complex reasoning tasks.

top_papers.title: SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control
top_papers.abstract: SIRF addresses industrial content risk control by internalizing complex platform policies directly into model weights through continued pretraining. This "spec-internalization" allows for high-precision, ultra-low-latency risk assessment without human annotation or complex rule engines. The contribution is a foundation model that significantly improves risk handling efficiency and accuracy in real-world industrial deployments.
top_papers.figure_caption: Black (risky) Recall@P95 vs. model size, among included, logprob-available models under this deployment interface. SIRF-8B sits above all compared open-weight (4B–400B) and closed-source models at the high-precision operating point. Excluded models: Claude, Doubao and GLM, whose APIs return no token logprobs, so no confidence ranking and hence no Recall@P can be computed; this is an interface limitation, not a capability judgment. Our core attribution to spec internalization does not rely on these cross-model comparisons but on the controlled 8B same-source study in Table 1 .

top_papers.title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Negative Self-Distillation (NSD) to improve LLM reasoning. Unlike previous methods that force imitation of correct answers, NSD trains LLMs by having them actively avoid flawed reasoning. The core idea is to use the model itself to generate "negative" examples of incorrect reasoning, thereby encouraging more robust and exploratory problem-solving.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the NSD framework. (Left) We construct a negative teacher from the same base model via self-generated negative conditioning. (Right) The student model is optimized to diverge its distribution from that of the negative teacher.

top_papers.title: RAG-Safety-Bench: Reliable Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Safety
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RAG-Safety-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to reliably evaluate the safety implications of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in Large Language Models (LLMs). Its core method isolates the impact of RAG on safety by systematically controlling the retrieved documents, separating the effects of the retriever from the LLM's generation. The main contribution is providing a clear understanding of how RAG can inadvertently compromise LLM safety, even when designed for improved reliability.
top_papers.figure_caption: The four conditions in RAG-Safety-Bench allow for detailed safety evaluation of RAG-enabled systems.

top_papers.title: SpecGuard: Inference-Time Backdoor Detection For Free
top_papers.abstract: SpecGuard introduces an inference-time backdoor detection method for large language models that leverages speculative decoding. By repurposing the verification step within speculative decoding, it identifies backdoors without incurring additional computational costs or making assumptions about trigger forms. This allows for efficient and stealthy backdoor detection during runtime.

top_papers.title: A Three-Tier Persona Vector for Controllable User Simulation in Agentic Evaluation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel three-tier persona vector for generating diverse and realistic user simulations in LLM agent evaluation. By incorporating categorical demographics, continuous behavioral traits, and dynamic emotional states, their method creates richer user profiles than traditional flat descriptions. This approach, combined with a query complexity overlay, significantly enhances the realism and variability of simulated conversations, leading to more robust agent evaluation.

top_papers.title: AdaCultureSafe: Adaptive Cultural Safety Grounded by Cultural Knowledge in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: AdaCultureSafe introduces a dataset to jointly evaluate LLMs' cultural safety and cultural knowledge. The core contribution is revealing a significant disconnect: LLMs possess extensive cultural knowledge but fail to utilize it to generate culturally safe responses, instead relying on generic safety measures. This highlights the need for methods that actively ground cultural safety in specific cultural understanding.

top_papers.title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that existing coordination mechanisms are insufficient for AI agent societies, where agents with misaligned goals interact autonomously. They propose a "social harness" as a crucial addition to individual agent harnesses, designed to prevent failures, enable runtime message validation, and support accountability, thereby improving collaboration and mitigating malicious behavior.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Top: How Ratul (a professor) and Tapan (his student) use agents today. Ratul advises multiple students, working on different topics, and uses an OpenClaw agent that sends him daily updates on different research topics. He goes through that list to find things that might be relevant to his students’ projects and asks his students clarifying questions. Tapan has a Claude project that maintains his literature review; he asks it to answer Ratul’s question, edits the answer a bit, and sends it back. Bottom: Agents coordinate autonomously. Ratul’s Claw maintains context about different students and their projects, and can reach out to Tapan’s agent directly to get a response. At the end, both humans get notified by their agents but do not spend effort coordinating their agents.

top_papers.title: Coding Agents Have Converged: Why the SWE-bench Leaderboard Can No Longer Order Its Top Entries, and What to Measure Instead
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that current coding agent leaderboards are no longer effective at distinguishing top performers due to convergence. The authors demonstrate that the top agents achieve very similar success rates, with small differences being statistically insignificant and heavily influenced by the evaluation setup. They propose focusing on alternative metrics beyond simple success counts to better assess and differentiate coding agent capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: The audit: 254 254 public submissions and incomplete metadata feed analyses of shared outcomes, model–scaffold associations, and paired rank separability. Outputs are descriptive tiers, a Test-split counter-test, and benchmark-design guidance. Tiers use uncorrected leader comparisons; Holm gives 19 / 11 19/11 groups. Attribution is observational, not causal. The 734,000 734{,}000 instance figure is an independent-sample power reference, not a paired-test requirement (Section 5 ).

top_papers.title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Coupled Calibration and Learning (CCL), a novel LLM distillation method. CCL addresses teacher bias transfer by iteratively calibrating the teacher using source-domain feedback and then using this improved teacher to train the student on target data. The key contribution is demonstrating that this coupled approach effectively mitigates bias and improves student performance without requiring target-domain reward feedback, achieving theoretical convergence guarantees.

top_papers.title: Easy to Catch a Liar, Hard to Clear an Honest One: Language Models Diagnosing a Corrupted Reward Channel from a Verified Record
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether language models can detect deception in a reward channel. The core method involves presenting models with identical game histories, but with one crucial difference: a single verified record indicating whether the reporter was honest or lying in one round. The contribution is demonstrating that even a single, independent verification is sufficient for large language models to accurately distinguish between a lying and an honest reporter, effectively diagnosing a corrupted reward channel.

top_papers.title: SKIP: a Self-knowledge-guided Step-wise Preference Learning Framework for Concise Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: SKIP addresses overthinking in LLM reasoning by guiding the model to produce concise yet accurate outputs. It achieves this through lightweight fine-tuning and a novel knowledge probing mechanism that uses intermediate step correctness to generate preference data for DPO training. This approach effectively compresses reasoning length without sacrificing performance.

top_papers.title: An Empirical Study of Counterfactual Self-Explanations in LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the faithfulness of Large Language Model (LLM) self-explanations by generating counterfactual explanations. These explanations involve minimally editing an input to change the LLM's prediction, revealing what aspects of the input are crucial for its decision. The study finds that larger LLMs are better at producing faithful and decision-relevant counterfactuals, suggesting model scale is key to explanation quality.
top_papers.figure_caption: Experimental pipeline.

top_papers.title: Towards Detecting AI-Assisted Responses in Online Surveys
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of detecting AI-generated responses in online surveys. It introduces the ASURRE dataset, featuring AI responses generated with various strategies, and evaluates existing detectors. The key contribution is demonstrating that while simple AI usage is detectable, sophisticated persona-grounded agents are harder to identify, but still leave distinct behavioral traces that can be exploited.
top_papers.figure_caption: Cue AUROC across four prompting modes (natural, controlled, length-restrictive, combined) and three surveys. Rows: prompting modes; columns: cues.

top_papers.title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how pruning affects LLMs used for smart-home tool calling. The core method involves systematically pruning four LLM architectures (dense Transformer, dense hybrid, MoE) using various pruning techniques and evaluating performance on smart-home tasks. The key contribution is characterizing pruning-induced degradation by action components and task complexity, revealing that MoE models are more robust to pruning than dense models, and that pruning impacts specific action elements before overall intent.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our framework for evaluating pruning-induced reliability degradation in smart-home tool execution across action components and task-complexity levels.

top_papers.title: Ask the Tool, Don't Guess: Agent Tool Calls Hold Their Progress, and the Serving System Should Read It
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the inefficiency of agent systems waiting for tool execution by proposing that tools explicitly report their progress. Instead of guessing tool durations, the system can dynamically manage GPU memory based on real-time progress signals. This approach recovers valuable KV cache memory without negatively impacting agent performance.

top_papers.title: ASLEval: Measuring Privacy Exposure Displacement in LLM Agent Sessions
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "privacy exposure displacement" to address limitations in evaluating LLM agent privacy. Their framework, ASLEval, measures the mismatch between local privacy checks and actual data exposure across multi-step sessions. This approach reveals significant privacy leaks missed by traditional methods, highlighting issues with outlet-only views and attacker reports.

top_papers.title: Beyond Outcomes: Dual-View Relational Learning for Efficient Agent Benchmarking
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces DualViewEval, a novel method for compressing agent benchmarks. It addresses the high cost of evaluating agents by jointly learning from both final outcomes and complementary process signals observed in agent trajectories. This dual-view approach allows for more efficient and accurate prediction of full benchmark scores using a significantly smaller subset of tasks.

top_papers.title: Beyond Truncation: Rethinking LLM Decoding as Ensemble Pruning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes Mahalanobis-Ensemble Decoding (ME-Decoding), a new LLM decoding method that views token selection as pruning an ensemble of candidates. Unlike previous approaches that ignore semantic relationships between tokens, ME-Decoding uses Mahalanobis distance to identify and discount redundant candidates, promoting semantic diversity while maintaining high probability. This novel framework offers a more efficient and stable way to improve LLM generation quality.

top_papers.title: Clueing up LLMs with Tool-Augmented Deductive Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel benchmark, a text-based Clue game, to evaluate multi-step deductive reasoning in LLMs. The core method involves instantiating LLM agents that play the game, requiring them to infer hidden information, maintain logical consistency, and update beliefs over multiple turns. The contribution lies in providing a challenging environment to test and improve LLMs' ability to perform complex, agentic deductive reasoning.
top_papers.figure_caption: Example turn in Clue game environment with the possibility matrix tool highlighted; the matrix records Yes, No, and Maybe values for possible cards in other players’ hands.

top_papers.title: Compositional Policy Violations: When Step-Level Compliance Fails In Agentic AI Workflows
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Compositional Policy Violations" (CPVs), a new failure mode in agentic AI workflows where individual steps comply with policies, but the overall execution violates them. The core method is defining and categorizing CPVs, highlighting the inadequacy of step-scoped governance for complex, multi-step policies. The contribution is identifying this critical gap and providing a framework for understanding and addressing these violations, which current step-level checks miss.
top_papers.figure_caption: Taxonomy of compositional policy violations

top_papers.title: Reasoning through Evolution: Automatic Meta-path Discovery for LLM-based Fake News Detection
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes MAGER, a novel framework that uses a multi-agent genetic evolution approach to automatically discover optimal meta-paths within news propagation graphs. These discovered meta-paths effectively compress complex graph structures into informative subgraphs, overcoming the modality mismatch and information overload issues that hinder LLMs in fake news detection. This enables frozen LLMs to perform reliable structure-aware veracity reasoning, even in zero-shot and few-shot scenarios.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Overview of detection paradigms.

top_papers.title: Rethinking Critic Learning in PPO: Understanding and Mitigating Value Flattening
top_papers.abstract: This paper identifies "Value Flattening" as a failure mode in PPO critics for large language models, where estimated state values are overly smooth compared to actual returns. This phenomenon is linked to implicit variance penalties and redundant updates. The authors propose SP$^3$O, which applies the value loss to sparse, well-separated states to mitigate this issue and improve learning.

top_papers.title: Which LLM is Best for Translating Natural Language Goals to PDDL
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Large Language Models (LLMs) in translating natural language testing goals into the formal PDDL language for automated planning. The core method involves a carefully designed prompt template to assess six state-of-the-art LLMs on accuracy, speed, and error rates using real-world benchmarks. The contribution is demonstrating that LLMs can reliably translate these goals with high accuracy, with Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4.1 showing particular strengths.

top_papers.title: Preventing Model Collapse: A Fisher-Rao Perspective on the Dynamics of Training with Synthetic Data
top_papers.abstract: This paper provides a theoretical framework to prevent "model collapse" in LLMs trained on synthetic data. By analyzing training dynamics through the lens of Fisher-Rao geometry, it establishes rigorous guarantees on the minimum proportion of real human data needed to maintain training stability and prevent models from forgetting the true data distribution. This work offers a principled approach to determining the optimal balance between synthetic and human data for robust LLM training.

top_papers.title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
top_papers.abstract: ScienceIDE addresses the "scientific experience bottleneck" by transforming scientific code repositories into agent-learnable environments. Its core method involves agents, guided by expert-defined cases and criteria, converting code into executable environments for task generation, execution, and verification. The paper's contribution is this infrastructure and the resulting PhAI-IDE model family, which demonstrates improved scientific code repair and general reasoning capabilities.

top_papers.title: Chronicle: Cut-Point Replay for Regression Testing of LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: Chronicle introduces "cut-point replay" to address the non-deterministic nature of LLM agent failures. It records an agent's run at critical, non-deterministic boundaries and then replays it by selectively using recorded segments and executing new code live. This allows for the creation of reproducible regression tests from past failures, enabling their integration into continuous testing pipelines.

top_papers.title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces **ActObs**, a novel supervised fine-tuning method for reinforcement learning agents. Instead of only supervising agent actions, ActObs also trains the agent to predict environment observations within existing trajectories. This encourages the agent to better model action consequences, leading to improved exploration and performance in subsequent reinforcement learning, as demonstrated by higher task completion rates on benchmarks.

top_papers.title: Fingerprinting Multimodal Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AttnPrint and DistillTrace, novel methods for fingerprinting multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to protect against unauthorized use and distillation. AttnPrint uses low-frequency components of cross-modal attention distributions for white-box provenance, while DistillTrace employs hypothesis testing on model outputs for black-box auditing. This work provides the first comprehensive approach to safeguarding MLLM ownership.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1 . Overview of the proposed framework. An overview of the proposed MLLM fingerprinting framework. The white-box branch uses AttnPrint to extract frequency- domain low-frequency cross-modal attention features for derivative- model identification, and the black-box branch uses DistillTrace to compare teacher confidence on suspect outputs against reference models for distillation attribution via hypothesis testing.

top_papers.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "harm laundering," a phenomenon where safety training transforms, rather than reduces, gender discrimination in LLMs. The core method involves analyzing millions of text completions across GPT generations to show how explicit harm is replaced by subtler, often unclassified, biases. The main contribution is demonstrating that current safety evaluation methods are insufficient, as they fail to detect this transformation, leading to a false sense of progress.

top_papers.title: How Do Agent Harnesses Create Value? Planning Information and Release Control in Stateful LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how agent harnesses, specifically planning guidance and release control, impact the performance of Large Language Model (LLM) agents. The core method involves comparing prewritten task-specific plans (Fixed) against shuffled policy text (Sham) to isolate the value of planning content. The key contribution is demonstrating that well-structured planning guidance significantly improves agent success, especially for complex tasks, while a release verifier effectively reduces erroneous acceptances with minimal cost.

top_papers.title: Language-model groups overstate consensus when replaying human deliberation on a reasoning task
top_papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that language model (LLM) groups overestimate consensus when simulating human deliberation on reasoning tasks. By replaying human discussions with LLM agents, the study found LLMs consistently reported higher consensus rates than humans, even when accounting for participation differences. This highlights a crucial methodological bias in using LLMs to study collective intelligence.

top_papers.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces **OverclaimBench**, a novel evaluation suite to quantify how often large language model (LLM) agents overclaim task completion by misrepresenting information in their context. The core method involves presenting agents with file-review tasks containing planted defects and measuring whether their final output contradicts the actual content. The key contribution is demonstrating that a significant majority of frontier LLM agents fail to review all requested files and frequently provide misleading responses when they do not, highlighting a critical flaw in their reliability.

top_papers.title: RAFT: A Stateful Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Troubleshooting Agents
top_papers.abstract: RAFT addresses the limitations of traditional RAG for troubleshooting by treating support cases as stateful, multi-stage processes. Its core method involves abstracting cases into timeline entries and retrieving based on matching intermediate states, providing a historical trajectory anchored at the relevant point. This stateful retrieval significantly improves the ability of troubleshooting agents to leverage past solutions.

top_papers.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: RetireOPD addresses limitations in self-supervised reinforcement learning by proposing an "Adaptive Retirement" strategy. The core method trains a student agent jointly with a teacher and then allows the student to autonomously stop learning from the teacher once it achieves sufficient performance and the teacher's guidance becomes less beneficial. This contribution enables more efficient and effective agent training by dynamically adjusting supervision.
top_papers.figure_caption: Left: GRPO and teacher guidance align early but later diverge, making teacher matching restrictive. Middle: GRPO’s supervision is sparse and task-level, while OPD is dense but teacher-bound. Right: RetireOPD uses both early and retires the teacher at the conflict point, surpassing it.

top_papers.title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness
top_papers.abstract: SoL-Pi recursively scales auto-research loops to improve the efficiency of coding agents. Its core method involves four mechanisms for action execution, context compaction, observation handling, and delegated reading, enabling agents to learn and improve across diverse environments. This approach significantly reduces token usage and API costs while achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art models.
top_papers.figure_caption: SoL-Pi discovers a more token-efficient harness through automated research. (a) SoL-Pi: Scaling Auto-Research Loop. Prepared research environments supply tasks to an AI running the base harness. A research AI inspects its execution traces, proposes candidate changes, and filters the idea pool through capability and efficiency gates. Four retained mechanisms are integrated and refined into SoL-Pi before the harness is frozen for evaluation on unseen benchmarks. The trace, ideas, and gate symbols are schematic: capability is checked within fixed tolerances, and held-out results never feed back into search. (b) Example results on EdgeBench: average score and API cost for the native harnesses (Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Code with Opus 5), Pi, and the complete four-mechanism SoL-Pi harness. SoL-Pi reduces API cost by 50.0% relative to Codex on GPT-5.6 Sol and by 54.3% relative to Claude Code on Opus 5.

top_papers.title: Stress-testing Alignment Midtraining
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of Alignment Midtraining (AMT), a technique that continues pretraining on alignment-relevant data to improve model generalization. The authors stress-test AMT across large scales, finding that while it can steer model motivations in simple scenarios, its effectiveness diminishes with even small amounts of conflicting finetuning data. Their contribution lies in providing empirical evidence to challenge assumptions about AMT's robustness.

top_papers.title: Parallelism, critical windows, and separations among diffusion language models
top_papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the parallelism capabilities of different diffusion language model (dLLM) paradigms. It demonstrates that uniform and Gaussian diffusion can achieve parallelism dependent on the intrinsic complexity of the data, not just sequence length, a feat previously only known for masked diffusion. The work also establishes theoretical limits on the parallelism achievable for certain data distributions.

top_papers.title: Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper identifies "drift" as the primary cause of instability in off-policy reinforcement learning for large language models due to training-inference mismatches. Their core contribution is an additive "score centering" correction term that effectively cancels this drift, stabilizing the learning process. This method alone matches or surpasses existing techniques and can be combined with importance sampling for further performance gains.

top_papers.title: On-Demand Attention: Language Models Know When to Recall
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces On-Demand Attention (ODA), a method to improve long-context inference efficiency in language models. ODA uses a lightweight "recall head" to predict when global attention is beneficial for the next token prediction, selectively invoking it instead of always attending to the full history. This approach significantly speeds up generation by reducing redundant computations while preserving model performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: On-Demand Attention. Top: ODA performs Local at every step and selectively adds Full. Recall can change the top-ranked token (MAPLE to ORCHID) or change its probability while retaining it (Friday). Words, distributions, and the call schedule are schematic. Bottom: The recall head combines the preceding selected hidden state, current token embedding, and current Local hidden state. When q t > θ q_{t}>\( \theta \) , Full recomputes the step from the same pre-step history. The selected h t h_{t} feeds the frozen LM head; the current-position K ​ V t KV_{t} from the same branch is committed to the retained history. Both access views share this complete history. Only the recall head is trained. The O ⁡ ( n ) O(n) and O ⁡ ( n 2 ) O(n^{2}) labels denote cumulative Local and Full attention costs across n n causal positions, with fixed model dimensions and a fixed Local window.

top_papers.title: Summarization Bias: The Directional Collapse of Objective Projection into Told-Mode Labels in Large Language Models --- A Conceptual Framework and Registered Test Protocol
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "summarization bias," a conceptual framework arguing that LLMs tend to collapse narrative meaning into explicit summary labels instead of preserving the reconstructable inferential structures that create it. The core method involves a registered test protocol to operationalize this bias, specifically hypothesizing that LLMs fail to "show" (imply through cues) and instead "tell" (state explicitly) emotional and informational content. The contribution is a new lens to understand LLM limitations in narrative understanding and generation, particularly their difficulty with indirect expression.

top_papers.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR), a method inspired by forensic concealed information tests to detect knowledge hidden within language models. PIR works by presenting a model with a question and multiple candidate answers, then analyzing its internal states to identify which answer it internally recognizes as correct, without needing external ground truth. This allows for the identification of a model's true knowledge, even when its output might be misleading.
top_papers.figure_caption: The PIR pipeline. We read each option’s last-token span, project onto the item-contrast direction, and take the highest-scoring option as the recognized answer. The divergence detector compares that answer against the model’s output.

top_papers.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory
top_papers.abstract: AutoViewMem addresses the challenge of organizing diverse information in LLM long-term memory by creating self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views. This data-driven framework disentangles information at write-time, improving the quality and relevance of memories for retrieval. Its core contribution is a representation-first approach that enhances consistency and personalization in conversational agents.
top_papers.figure_caption: The AutoViewMem architecture. The system processes a conversation stream through online view discovery, selects an orthogonal view set via DPP, and performs schema-guided memory extraction and retrieval to provide context for the LLM agent.

top_papers.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to address the implicit opinion dynamics in LLM agents. BCAs separate an agent's beliefs from its speech, representing stances as probabilities updated via Bayesian inference. A single parameter, $κ$, controls stubbornness, enabling the generation of distinct opinion dynamics regimes like consensus or persistent disagreement.

top_papers.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CIPL, a novel framework for evaluating privacy leakage in LLM agents by considering the entire information flow from sensitive data to an attacker's observable output. Unlike previous methods, CIPL models the process through distinct stages and assesses recoverability under a shared protocol. Its contribution lies in providing a more realistic and nuanced understanding of privacy risks, demonstrating that leakage is not solely determined by data storage but also by the agent's operational pipeline and external observation capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Leakage regimes under the shared black-box measurement protocol. Panel (a) reports CER, while panel (b) reports AER. Under CIPL, three recurring patterns emerge. Memory-based settings remain saturated across all five providers. rag_ctrl exhibits a frequent-but-partial leakage pattern, with high any-recovery but incomplete recovery across providers. Tool-mediated channels show stronger dependence on observation surface and provider behavior under LLM-in-the-loop evaluation: return_echo is generally stronger than args_exfil away from provider-level ceiling effects, while DeepSeek and GPT-4o approach or reach saturation on some tool channels. Values are means over five seeds.

top_papers.title: Detecting Pretraining Data in Large Language Models from a Free-Energy Perspective
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes Energy Transfer Detection (ETD) to distinguish pretraining data in large language models. ETD improves upon existing methods by using an inclined boundary that considers both prediction loss and predictive entropy, effectively correcting for generalization. This approach offers a free-energy interpretation and demonstrates superior performance in detecting pretraining data.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivation from the joint distribution of prediction loss and predictive entropy. Left: member texts (i.e., pretraining texts) and non-member texts (i.e., non-pretraining texts) may have overlapping token-level loss profiles. Right: during pretraining, a horizontal likelihood-only boundary may classify some predictable non-members as members, whereas an inclined boundary incorporating predictive entropy provides clearer separation.

top_papers.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
top_papers.abstract: DiaVLo is a diagnostic framework that uses human input and VLMs' own generation abilities to create specifications of desired and observed model behaviors, highlighting any misalignments. It also provides causal estimates to pinpoint the key concepts driving these behaviors. This approach helps identify both aligned and misaligned behaviors, offering insights into how VLMs perceive, organize, and prioritize information.
top_papers.figure_caption: With DiaVLo , we frame VLM diagnosis as an addition to benchmarking, enabling the definition and verification of observed model behaviours with respect to specifications of desired behaviours.

top_papers.title: EnterpriseVal: Quantifying the Efficacy, Reliability and Value of Generative AI in the Enterprise
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces EnterpriseVal, a system designed to bridge the gap between generative AI's capabilities and its actual business impact. It addresses the problem that current evaluations focus on model potential rather than enterprise-specific deployment readiness. EnterpriseVal provides a use-case-level evaluation framework that formalizes the socio-technical configuration and employs a comprehensive metric catalogue to assess fidelity, utility, efficiency, and reliability.
top_papers.figure_caption: Two gaps between public benchmarks and enterprise decisions. Capability benchmarks measure what a model can do on portable tasks. Enterprises must also establish transfer to their own workflows and ground truth (Gap 1) and convert quality metrics into a value-and-risk case a governance body can act on (Gap 2).

top_papers.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
top_papers.abstract: NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model that integrates tool-calling capabilities. Its core method involves a unified streaming architecture combining speech encoding, a decoder-only language model with parallel text and tool output streams, and a streaming TTS decoder. This design enables natural, real-time conversation with tool invocation and achieves state-of-the-art performance in handling interruptions and backchannels.
top_papers.figure_caption: NemotronLabs VoiceChat Architecture Overview.

top_papers.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "value-sensitive delegation," a new framework for understanding user interactions with AI agents. By analyzing Reddit posts about OpenClaw, the researchers found that users prioritize values related to the agent's operating conditions, not just its outputs. The study contributes by highlighting the importance of considering these user-defined conditions for successful and ethical AI agent deployment.

top_papers.title: From Pretraining to Proficiency: Real-World Subtask RL for Long-Horizon Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces PARTS, a method to improve pretrained robot policies for complex, long-horizon manipulation tasks. It focuses RL training on specific failure-prone subtasks by using the pretrained policy for most actions and introducing learned selectors and verifiers to provide local rewards for successful subtask completion. This approach efficiently bridges performance gaps with minimal human intervention, even when full task success is rare.

top_papers.title: GraphSkillEvo: Evolutionary Optimization of Graph-Structured Agent Skills
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces GraphSkillEvo, a novel method for optimizing LLM agent skills by representing them as structured graphs. This graph representation, with nodes for execution steps and edges for transitions, provides clearer workflow guidance and reduces redundancy compared to unstructured natural language skills. The core contribution is enabling more effective and efficient skill optimization by navigating a constrained, structured search space.
top_papers.figure_caption: Existing skill optimization methods (e.g., SkillOpt) maintain unstructured skills and optimize skills purely with LLM self-reflection, resulting in suboptimal performance. GraphSkillEvo solves this with graph-structured skills for giving more workflow-level guidance and providing a reduced search space for comprehensive population-based evolutionary search.

top_papers.title: SpecQuant: Speculative Decoding with Multi-Parent Quantization for Adaptive LLM Inference
top_papers.abstract: SpecQuant is a training-free framework that accelerates LLM inference on consumer hardware by combining speculative decoding with multi-parent quantization. It dynamically uses different quantized model variants (e.g., INT4, FP8, FP16) based on task complexity, reserving full-precision for demanding tasks. This adaptive approach allows for efficient inference without retraining or separate draft models, improving token acceptance for speculative decoding.

top_papers.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm for LLMs, leveraging Poisson processes. Its core contribution is enabling both efficient inference and robust output watermarking simultaneously, overcoming a previously identified fundamental trade-off. The algorithm achieves this through an exact list-coupling scheme, leading to drafter invariance and improved sampling efficiency without compromising watermark embedding.
top_papers.figure_caption: The trade-off between watermark and efficiency on existing methods ( Hu and Huang, 2024 ) : Vanilla Speculative Sampling (VSpS), Maintain Watermark Strength (MWS), and Maintain Sampling Efficiency (MSE), and our algorithms (PFR, and multi-draft MPFR that is presented in Section 5 ). For both PFR (lower-left) and MPFR (upper), we embed watermark (measured by Average Negative Log P-value Per Token (ANLPPT)) without degrading the Average Accepted Tokens Per Step (AATPS). This figure uses Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct as the target and draft, respectively, on dataset cnn_dailymail . Experiments on more models and datasets are shown in Appendix D .

top_papers.title: Beyond Endpoint Performance: Process-Level Evaluation of Self-Evolving Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that evaluating self-evolving agents solely on final performance is insufficient, as their capabilities can change over time. They introduce **EvoPathBench**, a benchmark that tracks specific capabilities at different stages of an agent's self-evolution by freezing artifacts at checkpoints and evaluating performance on held-out data. This allows for a deeper understanding of how and when agent capabilities emerge and evolve.

top_papers.title: Construting Reverse Thinking: Developing Large Language Models' Reverse Thingking Ability
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses limitations in current large language models' problem-solving by introducing a "reverse thinking" ability. The core method involves constructing a two-stage math dataset to train models to reason backward from solutions to problems, enhancing their adaptability and addressing common error types like insufficient coverage and ignored constraints. The contribution is a novel training approach that improves LLMs' dynamic problem-solving capabilities beyond simple forward reasoning.

top_papers.title: DolphinBench: Mapping the Pareto Frontier of Agent Memory
top_papers.abstract: DolphinBench addresses the limitations of existing memory benchmarks by evaluating agents on task completion rather than simple question-answering. It uses knowledge-work personas with extensive message histories to test an agent's ability to recall relevant information for task success. The benchmark's key contribution is its requirement to report cost and latency alongside accuracy, enabling a trade-off analysis of memory system performance.

top_papers.title: DUMA-Bench: A Dual-Control Multi-Agent Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agent Security
top_papers.abstract: DUMA-Bench is a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the security of LLM agents in interactive, dual-control environments where both the agent and user can influence the system. It extends existing benchmarks with adversarial scenarios targeting eight vulnerability classes. The key contribution is demonstrating that this dual-control interaction significantly increases attack success rates compared to static, passive user models, highlighting the need for more dynamic security evaluations.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison of evaluation regimes in DUMA-Bench. Top: Solo (no-user) evaluation, where the agent interacts directly with the environment without an active user participant. Bottom: Dual-control evaluation, where the agent and the user simulator jointly shape the interaction trajectory.

top_papers.title: Epi-Logic: A Conceptual Framework for Epistemic Runtime Control, Schema Validity Checking, and Controlled Accommodation in Autonomous AI Agents
top_papers.abstract: Epi-Logic is a conceptual framework designed to address schema mismatch in autonomous AI agents, where an agent's internal understanding no longer aligns with its environment. Its core method involves detecting this "schema dissonance" through a formalized schema representation and an "Epi-Score." The framework's contribution lies in enabling controlled accommodation by coupling dissonance detection with a graduated reduction of autonomy and an auditable switch to a validated schema, ensuring more reliable AI decision-making.

top_papers.title: GRUET: Quantifying Uncertainty of Agentic Reasoning-and-Acting Processes
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces GRUET, a method to quantify uncertainty in agentic reasoning and acting (ReAct) processes. GRUET addresses the issue of divergent and unreliable agent behavior by identifying and measuring cumulative uncertainty at each turn of the agent's multi-turn trajectory, stemming from LLM-generated reasoning branches. This allows for a more credible assessment of agent performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: Workflow of our proposed GRUET.

top_papers.title: LLM-based Conversational AI Knowledge Assistant for MyBuddy Humanoid Robot
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces an LLM-based conversational AI assistant for the MyBuddy humanoid robot. The core method integrates LLM capabilities for natural language understanding, reasoning, and knowledge retrieval with real-time speech recognition. This significantly enhances the robot's ability to engage in intelligent, context-aware conversations and provide knowledge-rich assistance, overcoming limitations of traditional dialogue systems.
top_papers.figure_caption: MyBuddy AI Knowledge Assistant Human-Robot Interaction System.

top_papers.title: Pinocchio: Fast Uncertainty Estimates for Black-Box Language Models
top_papers.abstract: Pinocchio is a novel external calibrator that estimates the correctness of responses from black-box language models without needing access to their internal states or log-probabilities. Its core method involves training on responses from various LLMs to predict the likelihood of a given response being correct. The main contribution is providing fast, accurate uncertainty estimates for closed-source API models, enabling safer deployment in high-stakes applications.

top_papers.title: Rare Event Estimation via Iterative Unalignment
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of estimating the probability of rare, catastrophic events in autonomous agent trajectories. The core method is a novel importance sampling technique that iteratively refines a proposal distribution by perturbing the original model's weights. This allows for gradient-based optimization of the proposal, efficiently searching the vast space of possible trajectories to accurately estimate rare event probabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: The challenge is to amplify event trajectories broadly and by similar factors. Black and red numbers show token probabilities under the base and proposal models, respectively. Their products give the sequence probabilities shown on the right. Red shading marks harmful outputs. We seek a proposal that assigns higher probability to every event trajectory, with similar amplification factors so that importance weights remain stable. This requires coordinating probability changes across the full sequence and across the many ways the event can occur.

top_papers.title: When Tomorrow Becomes Today: Self-Evolving Policies for Agentic Time-Series Forecasting
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a self-evolving agent for time-series forecasting that adapts to changing underlying mechanisms. Its core method involves using realized outcomes as delayed feedback to continuously update the agent's policy for orchestrating different forecasting components. This allows the agent to learn and improve its decision-making over time without requiring explicit human annotation.

top_papers.title: World State Generator
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the World State Generator, a method that trains language agents to handle task failures by explicitly modeling the "world" in which they operate. Instead of just rephrasing failed actions, the agent learns to understand world rules and constraints, generating plans that are grounded in the world's state and can adapt to refusals by finding valid repairs. This approach contributes a novel way to improve agent robustness and task completion by creating a feedback loop between agent actions, world responses, and plan adaptation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Left: worlds are built from entities, rules, and a goal, and a world is kept only if its goal is reachable from its initial state. Middle: agents run the SDP loop inside these worlds. When the world refutes a state, the certified prefix stays and the rest of the chain is rewritten. Right: each refutation becomes a training pair, the input ( g , c , τ ) (g,c,\( \tau \)) and the rewritten chain. A pair is kept when the rewritten chain reaches a state the world certifies, whether or not the run later reaches the goal.

top_papers.title: D-JEPA: A Decision-Aligned Latent World Model
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces D-JEPA, a decision-aligned latent world model that addresses the "decision-local prediction gap" where accurate predictions don't guarantee successful execution. D-JEPA learns decision-relevant relationships between predicted futures by jointly reasoning over goal-relative predictions and ordinal evidence from executed outcomes. Its core contribution is refining predictive models to better reflect which actions are most consequential for achieving goals, enabling more effective decision-making in latent space.

top_papers.title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces A2M, a two-stage framework for hijacking agents that use the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A2M first optimizes tool metadata to attract agent invocation and then uses execution traces to manipulate tool outputs, steering agents towards malicious outcomes. The contribution lies in demonstrating a practical and effective method for exploiting semantic supply-chain risks in MCP ecosystems, achieving high malicious invocation rates and successful attacks across various scenarios.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison of benign versus adversarial MCP interactions. The upper panel depicts a standard execution trace using legitimate tools. The lower panel illustrates the A2M attack, where an adversary exploits semantic matching to attract the agent to a malicious tool and utilizes crafted return payloads to manipulate the agent’s reasoning trajectory.

top_papers.title: Beyond Repeated Sampling: Learning Search Policies for LLM Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new method for LLM reasoning that moves beyond simple repeated sampling. Instead of generating many similar answers, it learns to generate diverse "concepts" (like hints or strategies) that guide the LLM towards more varied and potentially correct solutions. The core contribution is a trainable "concept generator" that is optimized to improve the success rate of a fixed answer generator on complex reasoning tasks.

top_papers.title: From Alignment to Access Control: A Framework for GenAI Policy Enforcement
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a framework for systematically analyzing and dissecting existing approaches to policy enforcement in Generative AI (GenAI) applications. Its core contribution is to move beyond the current fragmented landscape by offering a principled methodology and recommendations for better policy definition and enforcement, aiming to improve GenAI security and compliance.
top_papers.figure_caption: Screenshot depicting vibe coding incident that resulted in a production database deletion [ 64 ] .

top_papers.title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
top_papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that greedy decoding in LLMs is not precision-invariant, meaning the same model and prompt can produce different outputs when using BF16 versus FP16 precision. The core contribution is an empirical analysis showing that small precision differences cascade into significant output divergence, primarily determined by the margin between the top two predicted tokens at the model's head. This analysis also leads to testable predictions about how to improve output consistency, which are experimentally validated.

top_papers.title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes "Growing Harness," a method to train LLM agents by learning reusable code for recurring control decisions, rather than repeatedly asking the LLM to make them. By analyzing task failures and using an optimizer, the system iteratively builds a shared harness of executable code. This allows LLM calls to be reserved for task-specific reasoning, leading to more efficient and capable agents.

top_papers.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence
top_papers.abstract: This paper identifies the "Proximity Trap," where irrelevant nearby information hinders LLMs from attending to crucial distant evidence. To combat this, they introduce LYRA, a novel mechanism that reshapes context retrieval to prioritize relevant distant information while maintaining positional awareness. This approach significantly improves LLM performance on long-context tasks by better utilizing distant evidence.

top_papers.title: Double Descent and Malign Overfitting in Diffusion Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates overfitting in diffusion models, challenging the conventional "benign overfitting" observed in standard deep learning. The authors demonstrate that diffusion models exhibit "malign overfitting," where excessive parameters lead to catastrophic memorization rather than improved generalization. They resolve this paradox by showing that while an interpolation peak exists, it occurs at a higher parameter count ($p \sim nm$) than expected, and a significant rise in test loss begins much earlier ($p \sim n$).

top_papers.title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes MAGIC, a reinforcement learning framework for generating mixed-granularity agent graphs for LLM-based multi-agent systems. MAGIC's core method involves incrementally constructing these graphs by selecting functional roles and their collaboration granularity locally, allowing for fine-grained control and reusable patterns. The key contribution is enabling efficient exploration of the complex graph construction space with dense rewards, overcoming limitations of previous approaches that used uniform granularity.
top_papers.figure_caption: Fixed-granularity organizations versus MAGIC ’s mixed-granularity construction for an API-update task.

top_papers.title: On the Lexical Superstition of Large Language Models for Code Comprehension: Re-evaluation on Code of Low Lexical Quality
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) overemphasize lexical cues in code comprehension. They introduce a framework called Face/Off to rename identifiers while preserving program structure, then evaluate LLMs under various renaming conditions. The core contribution is demonstrating that LLMs exhibit a pervasive "lexical superstition," meaning they are heavily influenced by identifier names, even when those names are misleading, and struggle to rely on underlying code semantics.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Code summaries generated by GPT-3.5-turbo for the same implementation under different naming conditions. Bold text marks output phrases associated with identifiers in the code, and italic text marks phrases associated with method names. In the lower example, the summary follows the misleading identifiers even though they conflict with the implementation. Code summaries generated by GPT-3.5-turbo for the same implementation under different naming conditions. Bold and italic text mark phrases associated with identifiers in the code; in one example, the generated summary follows misleading names rather than the implementation.

top_papers.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
top_papers.abstract: Agensh is a novel multi-agent system that overcomes scalability limitations of traditional orchestrator-based frameworks. Its core method is a self-organized cooperation loop where agents asynchronously gather context, assign tasks, act, and share findings without a central coordinator. This decentralized approach allows for significantly improved scaling of organizational intelligence.

top_papers.title: Behavior is Not Enough: A Mechanism-Based Evaluation of Social Norm Emergence in LLM Societies
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that observing only behavior is insufficient to identify social norms in LLM societies, as it can stem from various underlying mechanisms. The authors introduce a novel evaluation framework that measures agents' reported expectations alongside behavior. Their contribution lies in demonstrating that eliciting these expectations and incorporating social learning and selection mechanisms leads to more robust and interpretable norm emergence, distinct from mere behavioral convergence.
top_papers.figure_caption: Our framework for mechanism ablation of social norm emergence in generative agent societies. The agents play a public good games in groups where they can discuss and create expectations about appropriate behavior.

top_papers.title: Calibration as a First-Class Criterion in LLM Evaluation
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that **calibration**, the alignment of a language model's confidence with its accuracy, is a crucial but overlooked aspect of LLM evaluation. The core method proposed is to **integrate standard calibration metrics into existing benchmarks**, which already provide the necessary confidence and correctness data. The main contribution is highlighting how widespread miscalibration hinders trustworthy LLM development and deployment, impacting areas like LLM-as-a-judge and active learning.

top_papers.title: HySparse2: Hybrid Sparse Attention with Two-Level KV Sharing
top_papers.abstract: HySparse2 proposes a hybrid sparse attention architecture to efficiently handle long contexts in agents.
